GEN.bio: Beginnings. Creation, the fall, a flood, and a family God refuses to give up on.

EXO.bio: Out of the house of bondage. Plagues, the Passover, a sea split open, the Law at Sinai, and a tent where God dwells.

LEV.bio: Be ye holy, because I the Lord your God am holy. Priests, sacrifices, the Day of Atonement, and a holy people.

NUM.bio: Forty years in the wilderness. Manna and murmuring, a bronze serpent, and a prophet hired to curse who can only bless.

DEU.bio: Moses' farewell on the edge of the promised land: remember, love the Lord with your whole heart, and choose life.

JOS.bio: Into the promised land. Jericho's walls fall, the tribes receive their portions, and a people chooses whom to serve.

JDG.bio: No king in Israel. Deborah, Gideon, Samson, and a cycle of falling away, crying out, and being rescued again.

RUT.bio: Loyal love in a time of famine. A Moabite widow, a barley field, and the great-grandmother of King David.

1SA.bio: Israel asks for a king. Hannah's prayer, Samuel's call, Saul's fall, and a shepherd boy who faces a giant.

2SA.bio: David's reign, in glory and in sin. Jerusalem taken, the ark brought home, and a promise of a throne forever.

1KI.bio: Solomon's wisdom and his temple, a kingdom torn in two, and Elijah meeting God in a whistling of a gentle air.

2KI.bio: Elijah's chariot of fire, Elisha's miracles, and two kingdoms sliding toward exile in Assyria and Babylon.

1CH.bio: History retold from Adam to David. Long genealogies, the ark carried up with songs, and plans for a temple.

2CH.bio: Solomon's temple and Judah's kings: revival and ruin, exile, then a Persian king tells God's people to go home.

EZR.bio: Home from Babylon. An altar rebuilt, a temple refounded amid shouts and tears, and a scribe devoted to the Law.

NEH.bio: A cupbearer rebuilds Jerusalem's walls in 52 days, work in one hand and a sword in the other. Then the Law is read.

TOB.bio: A blind father, a faithful son, an angel in disguise, a fish, a dog, and a marriage saved by prayer.

JDT.bio: A widow of Bethulia faces down an invading army with prayer, courage, and Holofernes' own sword.

EST.bio: An orphan turned queen of Persia risks her life before the king, and the lots cast for her people's ruin are reversed.

1MA.bio: Mathathias refuses the king's idols. Judas the Hammer and his brothers fight back, cleanse the Temple, free Judea.

2MA.bio: Eleazar, and a mother with her seven sons, die faithful. A purified Temple, prayer for the dead, hope of resurrection.

JOB.bio: A just man loses everything and argues with heaven. God answers from a whirlwind. "I know that my Redeemer liveth".

PSA.bio: Israel's prayer book: 150 songs of praise, lament, repentance and trust, prayed by synagogue and Church for millennia.

PRO.bio: Wisdom in small bites: work, words, money, friends. "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom."

ECC.bio: Vanity of vanities. Work, pleasure and wisdom weighed under the sun. The verdict: fear God and keep his commandments.

SOL.bio: A bride and her beloved among lilies and vineyards, read as human love and as God's love. For love is strong as death.

WIS.bio: Written in Solomon's name: wisdom as the brightness of eternal light, the just in God's hand, the Exodus retold.

SIR.bio: Jesus son of Sirach teaches the good life: friendship, speech, humility, family, and praise of "men of renown".

ISA.bio: Seraphim, a live coal, a virgin with child, and a Servant "wounded for our iniquities". Judgment, then comfort.

JER.bio: Called before birth to warn a city that would not listen. Tears, a yoke on his neck, and the promise of a new covenant.

LAM.bio: Five laments for a ruined Jerusalem, grief poured out to God. Yet his mercies are "new every morning".

BAR.bio: From Jeremiah's scribe in Babylon: confession, a hymn to wisdom, comfort for Jerusalem, Jeremiah's letter on idols.

EZE.bio: A priest in exile sees God's glory on wheels full of eyes. Dry bones live again, and hearts of stone become flesh.

DAN.bio: Faithful in exile: a fiery furnace, a lions' den, writing on the wall, Susanna saved, one like the son of man on clouds.

HOS.bio: A prophet's broken marriage becomes God's love letter to a faithless people: I will espouse thee to me for ever.

JOE.bio: Locusts strip the land. Then a call to rend your hearts, and a promise: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.

AMO.bio: A herdsman of Thecua takes on luxury and deceitful balances, and calls for justice as a mighty torrent.

OBA.bio: The Old Testament's shortest book. Proud Edom nests among the stars, and hears: thence will I bring thee down.

JON.bio: A runaway prophet, a storm, a great fish, and a God whose mercy is wide enough for Ninive. The prophet sulks.

MIC.bio: Swords into ploughshares, a ruler from little Bethlehem, and the plain answer to what the Lord requireth of thee.

NAH.bio: Comfort for Juda, doom for Ninive, the city of blood. The Lord is patient, but a tyrant's reckoning has come.

HAB.bio: How long, O Lord? A prophet argues with God, then waits on his watchtower. Answer: the just shall live in his faith.

ZEP.bio: That day is a day of wrath: the line behind the Dies irae. Then a humble remnant, and a God who rejoices over them.

HAG.bio: Your ceiled houses are done, God's house lies desolate. Consider your ways, rebuild the temple, and glory will fill it.

ZEC.bio: Night visions of horses, a golden candlestick and two olive trees. Then a king who comes poor, and riding upon an ass.

MAL.bio: Last of the twelve prophets. Lame sacrifices, broken faith, a messenger to prepare the way, and the Sun of justice.

MAT.bio: The Gospel of the kingdom. Jesus fulfils the prophets, preaches on the mount, and sends his disciples to all nations.

MAR.bio: The shortest Gospel, always in motion. Immediately Jesus heals, teaches, goes to the cross, and rises. Keep up.

LUK.bio: An orderly account for Theophilus: the manger, the Magnificat, the prodigal son, the good Samaritan, Emmaus.

JOH.bio: In the beginning was the Word. Seven signs, the I am sayings, the beloved disciple, and a love that lays down its life.

ACT.bio: Luke, part two. Wind and fire at Pentecost, then the Gospel runs from Jerusalem to Rome, shipwreck included.

ROM.bio: Paul's masterwork. All have sinned, grace did more abound, and nothing can separate us from the love of God.

1CO.bio: A divided church gets straight talk: factions, the Lord's Supper, gifts, the resurrection, and charity above all.

2CO.bio: Treasure in earthen vessels. Paul defends his ministry with tears and irony: power is made perfect in infirmity.

GAL.bio: Paul at full heat: there is no other gospel. Christ has made us free, so walk in the Spirit and bear its fruit.

EPH.bio: One Lord, one faith, one baptism. Grace that saves, the Church as Christ's body and bride, and the armour of God.

PHI.bio: A thank-you note written in chains that keeps saying rejoice. Christ emptied himself; every knee should bow.

COL.bio: Christ over all: the image of the invisible God, head of the body, the church. By him all things consist.

1TH.bio: Likely Paul's first letter. Hope for them that are asleep, and the trumpet of God at the Lord's coming.

2TH.bio: Don't panic: the day of the Lord is not here yet. Stand fast, hold the traditions, and keep working.

1TI.bio: Paul's charge to young Timothy: prayer, bishops and deacons, and the church, the pillar and ground of the truth.

2TI.bio: Paul's farewell from chains to his beloved son: guard what was entrusted, preach the word, finish the course.

TIT.bio: Left in Crete to set things in order: appoint presbyters, teach sound doctrine, live the grace that has appeared.

PHM.bio: A one-page plea from prison: take back Onesimus, not now as a servant, but instead of a servant, a most dear brother.

HEB.bio: Jesus, the great high priest, better than the angels and every sacrifice. A cloud of witnesses, and hope as an anchor.

JAM.bio: Be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only. Wisdom for trials, a bridled tongue, care for the poor, faith that works.

1PE.bio: To strangers dispersed and suffering: you are living stones, a kingly priesthood. Faith tried by the fire.

2PE.bio: Peter's farewell before laying away his tabernacle: climb from faith to charity, and look for new heavens.

1JO.bio: God is light. God is charity. To little children: let us not love in word, nor in tongue, but in deed, and in truth.

2JO.bio: The ancient writes to the lady Elect: walk in truth, love one another, and give no welcome to deceivers.

3JO.bio: The ancient to beloved Gaius: welcome the travelling brethren, follow what is good, and don't be a Diotrephes.

JUD.bio: Short and urgent: contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints. Ends in a doxology for all ages.

REV.bio: Seven churches, a slain Lamb on the throne, a dragon cast down, and all things made new. Come, Lord Jesus.
